title: Do Far-Right Populists (Really) Seem More Authentic?
abstract: Abstract: This study examines the perceived authenticity of German politicians during the 2024 state elections in Brandenburg, Saxony, and Thuringia using data from a two-wave survey panel. The results show that AfD politicians were not perceived as more authentic than incumbents, challenging the notion of a general authenticity advantage for far-right populists. However, AfD candidates enjoyed a relative authenticity advantage among their own supporters: AfD voters perceived their party’s candidates as more authentic than voters of other parties perceived their candidates. Perceived authenticity was positively associated with candidates’ voting propensity, highlighting its relevance for electoral preferences. Finally, authenticity ratings increased significantly for four of six candidates during the campaign, suggesting that perceptions of political authenticity can change over time.
